_doc: Star databases / index files the plate solvers need, with the field-of-view range each one is meant for. Ranges are the publishers' own: ASTAP's are from hnsky.org/astap.htm and the project's SourceForge notes; the astrometry.net table is the index scale list from astrometry.net/doc/readme.html, where the rule is that a useful index has skymarks 10% to 100% of the image field. Sizes are approximate download sizes, for the disk-space warning. Add entries by PR; keep astapDatabases sorted from widest to narrowest field.

astapDatabases.name: W08 (wide field)
astapDatabases.notes: All-sky / very wide lenses. ASTAP picks it automatically above 20 degrees.

astapDatabases.name: G05 (wide field)
astapDatabases.notes: Camera lenses and very short refractors.

astapDatabases.name: D05 (500 stars/deg2)
astapDatabases.notes: Smallest of the D series. Enough for short focal lengths, and the cheapest on disk.

astapDatabases.name: D20 (2000 stars/deg2)
astapDatabases.notes: Good default for typical astrograph fields.

astapDatabases.name: D80 (8000 stars/deg2)
astapDatabases.notes: Deepest of the D series, for the narrowest fields. 1.25 GB.

_astrometryDoc: index-42xx (Tycho-2) and index-52xx (Gaia DR2) share this scale numbering: the last two digits pick the skymark size band. A useful index has skymarks between 10% and 100% of the image field, and the COARSEST usable bands are both the cheapest and the fastest to solve with, so take those first and add finer ones only if the solve misses. Every band below is split into healpix tiles except 4208 and up; tiles and tileBytes are measured from the mirrors themselves (2026-08-10), not estimated, because a band can be anything from 130 kB to 17 GB and the operator has to see that before pressing Install.
_astrometrySeriesDoc: One series owns each band, so no band is ever fetched twice. Bands 0 to 6 come from Gaia DR2, which is the only catalogue dense enough for a field under a degree; 7 and up come from Tycho-2. 'tiles' is the number of healpix files the band is split into (0 = a single file) and 'bytes' is the measured total for the whole band. The Gaia files are the LITE build: half the size of the full one and what astrometry.net recommends for ordinary use.

astrometrySeries.name: Gaia DR2 (5200 series, LITE)
astrometrySeries.notes: Narrow fields, down to a couple of arcminutes. Hosted at NERSC: data.astrometry.net no longer carries the 5200 series and answers 404 for it.

astrometrySeries.name: Tycho-2 (4200 series)
astrometrySeries.notes: Half a degree and wider. Band 7 is split into 12 tiles; 8 and up are a single file each.
